title: My thoughts on AI after finishing this year's Epic Mega Jam
author: Venetian5
selftext:
Made a spontaneous decision to join this year’s Epic MegaJam. I worked solo for 4 days, and I wanted to share the result of this little endeavor. I think the result is fairly decent, but I’d love to see a 👍 or 👎 from fellow developers.



As you know, this jam sparked a lot of controversy because of how Epic encourages vibe coding. I took the opportunity to find out whether the “Trust Me Bro” AI influencers on X are telling the truth that anyone can now vibe code a game from a single prompt in one day. And I found the answer: obviously NOT. Even with access to Fable 5.2, GPT Astra, Meshy, ElevenLabs, MCPs, automation and whatnot, making games is still hard and takes a lot of effort, and tech influencers are full of shit as always.



But it’s a different kind of effort. Claude spewed out 32,000 lines of C++ and I’ve seen none of it. I barely touched the editor. Even the levels were prompted. It’s remarkable what Claude can do when it has access to Unreal’s MCP server. Not only that: I had it connect to Meshy and ElevenLabs to generate 3D and audio assets and import them straight into Unreal. The automated asset pipeline worked flawlessly most of the time. To be clear, I’m not talking about asset quality.



So what was I doing while Claude vibe coded my game? One thing only: playing the damn game. I think I spent more hours testing than anything else. Then I wrote more prompts to fine-tune all the gameplay knobs until the experience felt complete. Even during friends-and-family playtests on Discord, I relayed feedback to Claude and delivered updated builds within the same session. I guess I took on a hybrid role of project manager and QA. I could focus entirely on delivering The Product rather than the process. It was a new and interesting experience, but also a slightly bitter one.



It feels sad that 30 years of passion and experience in programming can fade into irrelevance so quickly. Even though LLMs can’t and won’t replace thinking people, it’s still something every developer will have to process. But anyway, it’s just a middle-aged man yelling at the prompt :)
